[42826 Introduction to Complex Systems Modelling | Subject description]
Credit points: 3

This microcredential demystifies complexity and complex systems, guiding you through the modelling of such systems, which traditional analytics can't fully decipher. Modelling and simulation become tools to understand unpredictable system behaviours and the potential effects of our interventions. With complex systems pervasive across natural, social, and technological domains, mastering their modelling is crucial. You'll learn to identify, classify, and select the most appropriate modelling approach for a given system, enhancing your analytical proficiency in handling real-world complexity.

[42826 Introduction to Complex Systems Modelling | Learning and teaching activities]
This subject uses supported online learning strategies. Self-paced online learning material, including appropriate readings and videos.

 Case studies help develop and reinforce the concept of complex systems and the techniques of modelling those. Students will learn about complex systems and their occurrence before studying ways to model them. Opportunities to reflect on the materials, engage in discussions and receive feedback are available throughout the modules.

 Regular online consultations at times nominated on CANVAS and moderated discussion boards enable clarification of issues and peer/expert support for learning. Feedback on assessments, will also be available through the LMS.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[42826 Introduction to Complex Systems Modelling | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Explain what complex systems are and classify them according to their characteristics. (C.1)
SLO2: Explain the role of models and simulations, and the key steps in modelling through a review of case studies involving applications of modelling of complex systems and analysis techniques. (B.1, D.1)
